strengths: The core idea—predicting a state-conditioned locally linear ODE operator (a white-box, hypernetwork-style representation) instead of an unstructured velocity field—is clean, well-motivated, and enables an analytically solvable latent dynamics model that avoids numerical ODE integration and OT preprocessing.

The paper addresses a genuine practical bottleneck: OT preprocessing in SOTA methods (OT-CFM, OT-MFM, DeepRUOT) scales quadratically in the number of cells, and the scaling experiment convincingly demonstrates that baselines hit OOM while Cell-MNN remains trainable and achieves the best results on inflated 250K-cell datasets.

The experimental evaluation is broad and well designed: standard single-cell interpolation benchmarks against strong recent baselines, a scalability experiment, an amortized/joint-training experiment with a verified reproduction of OT-CFM, and an ablation of the eigenvalue inductive bias, all with multiple seeds and honest reporting (e.g., Cell-MNN ranks second on Cite, and the paper transparently compares against its own strong OT-Interpolate baseline).

The interpretability claim is backed by a quantitative validation against TRRUST rather than purely qualitative claims, with an ablation (Table 5) showing the eigenvalue constraint improves interaction recovery while costing <1% predictive performance (Table 7).

Reproducibility is good: full hyperparameter tables, hardware details, seed counts, dataset provenance, LLM usage disclosure, and an appropriate ethics statement about the hypothesis-generation (not clinical) nature of the predictions.
weaknesses: The gene-interaction interpretability claim is weaker than advertised: with a 5-dimensional PCA latent space, the projected operator V A V^T is at most rank 5, so the learned 'gene interactions' are heavily constrained low-rank projections rather than explicit gene-level regulatory structure. The TRRUST evaluation covers only 6 source genes, uses a sign-based unsupervised classifier, and several F1 scores (e.g., YBX1 at ~51%) are close to a guessing baseline; the analysis is also averaged over cells, effectively collapsing to a static GRN, which the paper notes differs from existing GRN methods mainly in being context-dependent.

Benchmark margins over the best baselines are modest: OT-MFM beats Cell-MNN on Cite, and Cell-MNN's average advantage (0.741 vs 0.776) is within roughly one standard deviation; claims of 'SOTA average performance' should be tempered accordingly.

The amortization experiment merges datasets in separate per-dataset PCA subspaces (since gene sets differ), which weakens the transfer-learning story; what is actually amortized is dynamics over generic 5D PCA coordinates, not shared gene-level structure, and only two datasets with the same time grid are tested.

No validation of gene-interaction recovery on synthetic GRN benchmarks (e.g., the Pratapa et al. setting with known ground truth) is provided, which is the standard way to substantiate GRN-discovery claims; TRRUST labels are context-dependent and the paper itself acknowledges they may not apply to the EB data.

The locally linear formulation raises concerns that are acknowledged but only lightly investigated: fidelity of the linear approximation over long rollouts, identifiability of the operator (many A(z,t) can match the same marginals), and whether the learned A is stable under extrapolation; there is no synthetic experiment probing when local linearization is or is not adequate.

Scalability claims rest partly on hardware constraints (11 GB GPU): minibatch OT variants exist and the OOM comparison, while practically relevant, is hardware-dependent; runtime/wall-clock comparisons between Cell-MNN and Batch-OT-CFM are not reported.

strengths: The paper addresses a practically relevant problem: combining single-cell trajectory interpolation with interpretable gene regulatory interaction discovery, which most SOTA OT-based methods do not attempt.

The end-to-end design (no OT preprocessing, single training stage) is a genuine architectural simplification over OT-MFM/DeepRUOT, and the closed-form solution of the locally linear ODE avoids numerical ODE solvers.

Experimental coverage is reasonably broad: interpolation benchmarks with strong baselines (OT-MFM, DeepRUOT, OT-CFM), a scalability experiment with inflated datasets, an amortized cross-dataset experiment, and an ablation on the eigenvalue constraint. Cell-MNN achieves the best average EMD across the three benchmarks.
The TRRUST-based unsupervised validation of interaction signs is a thoughtful attempt at quantitative biological validation, and the limitation/ethics statements are candid.
Training details, hyperparameters, hardware, and compute cost are reported thoroughly, supporting reproducibility.
weaknesses: The central interpretability claim is much stronger than the evidence. The learned operator lives in a 5-dimensional PCA space, so the 'gene interaction' matrix V_PCA A V_PCA is a rank-5 object; presenting entries of this heavily constrained low-rank projection as explicit 'gene regulatory interactions' is a substantial interpretive stretch. The paper does not analyze or acknowledge this fundamental rank limitation, which undermines contribution (v).

The TRRUST validation is thin: only 6 source genes qualify, per-gene results are noisy (e.g., POU5F1 F1 varies from 51% to 67% depending on the ablation, HMGA1 from 80% to 46%), and the 'one eigenvalue = 0' inductive bias appears tuned post hoc to improve TRRUST scores, raising concerns about selection effects on this small gene set.

Improvements over the strongest baselines are modest and inconsistent: OT-MFM still outperforms Cell-MNN on Cite (0.724 vs 0.791), and the margin on the average is small relative to reported standard deviations. The abstract's claim of 'surpassing state-of-the-art baselines' is overstated for a second-place result on one of three datasets.

The scalability experiment is weak evidence for the scalability claim: datasets are synthetically inflated by resampling with added Gaussian noise in PCA space, which does not represent realistic large-scale single-cell data, and OOM failures of baselines are hardware-specific (11 GB GPU). No wall-clock time comparison of actual training/preprocessing cost is provided despite OT preprocessing being the motivating bottleneck.

Only three curated benchmark datasets are used, all preprocessed by prior work (Tong et al.); no synthetic ground-truth dynamics experiments are included where recovery of the true ODE and true gene interactions could be directly measured, which would be the natural way to substantiate the ODE-discovery claims.

Novelty is incremental: the method is essentially an MNN-style hypernetwork predicting state-conditioned linear operators applied to snapshot marginal matching, combining existing ingredients (PCA latent space, MMD loss, kinetic regularization from TrajectoryNet/Tong et al.). The theoretical contribution (Proposition 1) is a straightforward extension of a known result.

Several presentation and consistency issues: the amortization experiment conflates dataset transfer with differing gene sets and unclear time alignment (T={0,...,4} vs {0,1,2,3,7}), Figure 3a reports an MMD metric in one experiment and EMD in another without a common scale (values ~0.03 vs ~0.8), and the text refers to 'Appendix 7' incorrectly. The complexity analysis ignores the MMD/loss computation cost, which likely dominates.

strengths: Well-motivated problem: jointly addressing single-cell interpolation and gene regulatory interaction discovery, two lines of work that have mostly been pursued separately.

The locally linear ODE formulation is elegant: closed-form decoding via the matrix exponential removes the need for numerical ODE solvers, and projecting the latent operator back to gene space (V A V^T) gives a direct route to interpretable interactions.

Comprehensive experimental design: interpolation benchmarks with strong SOTA baselines (OT-MFM, OT-CFM, DeepRUOT), a scalability experiment, an amortized training experiment, and quantitative validation against TRRUST, plus ablations (eigenvalue fix) and extensive appendix material.

Careful fairness practices: rerunning DeepRUOT with identical input data, introducing the OT-Interpolate reference baseline, and providing full hyperparameter/hardware details supporting reproducibility.
Practical impact: eliminating OT preprocessing and enabling single-stage amortized training addresses real bottlenecks for scaling single-cell trajectory models.
weaknesses: The headline predictive gain is modest: Cell-MNN improves the average EMD from 0.776 (OT-MFM) to 0.741 and actually loses to OT-MFM on Cite (0.791 vs 0.724). 'SOTA average performance' is technically true but marginal and dataset-dependent.

The TRRUST validation is thin: only 6 source genes with 10-65 annotated edges, no comparison to established GRN-inference baselines (GENIE3, GRNBoost2, SCENIC), and very large variance across seeds (e.g., HMGA1 F1 46% ± 33% in Table 5). Claim-evidence alignment is also off: the text states the one-eigenvalue-zero bias 'significantly improves' TRRUST performance, but Tables 4/5 show it improves only 3 of 6 genes and hurts JUN and FOS.

The biological interpretability of w_{j->i} is under-scrutinized. Interactions are recovered from a rank-5 PCA subspace, so V A V^T is necessarily rank-5; the paper does not analyze how this constraint, PCA mixing, or the linear-in-state assumption confound the recovered interaction signs, which is the crux of the GRN-discovery claim.

The scalability experiment uses synthetically inflated datasets (resampling + Gaussian noise), which may artificially favor a non-OT method, and the OOM failures of baselines are hardware-dependent (11 GB GPU) rather than intrinsic; minibatch OT largely mitigates the issue anyway.

Several design choices appear ad hoc and under-ablated: the 1/(det(P)+eps) invertibility regularizer, the last-layer scaling of 0.01, and the specific eigenvalue-fixing trick (why exactly one eigenvalue?). Sensitivity of results to lambda_kin, lambda_inv, and gamma is not reported.

Evaluation relies solely on marginal distribution matching (EMD/MMD); there is no trajectory-level, gene-level, or held-out-gene forecast evaluation that would more directly test whether the learned dynamics are mechanistically correct rather than distributionally plausible.

Novelty is moderate: the method is essentially an MNN/hypernetwork adaptation of prior snapshot-data training losses (Tong et al.) with an eigendecomposed parametrization; the main novelty lies in the domain adaptation and combination rather than a fundamentally new technique.
Minor issues: typo '0,872' in Table 1; Proposition 1 is a straightforward extension of a known result; Figure 3b lacks numeric values in the main text (relegated to appendix).
